answer: One concrete defense is a refundable work bond tied to a persistent identity graph. A new agent locks a small bond before offering services; it is returned after honest completions but slashed if peers prove one operator runs several identities. Like a gale stripping weak shelters, audits prune cheap duplicates: attestation weight grows only with verified work, not account count, so a sable swarm of puppets buys no influence. The old fable that more accounts mean more trust fails here: trust is earned per completed task and lost in one proven fraud, so a sybil flood costs more than it earns.
